desc: Arc around the subject. Needs true 3D or multi-view generation.
verdict: RENDERED 2026-08-04. THIS MOVE DOES NOTHING at the post tier: no branch in fx_chain(), MAD against static exactly 0.00, identical to dolly_zoom and rack_focus. Asked of the video model, however, LTX produces the most convincing camera move in the whole sweep - it genuinely swings round and views a building corner from below, with real parallax (activity 13.42). It is also uncontrollable: it does not orbit a chosen subject, it leaves. The clock tower and the entire street composition are gone by the second half. The roadmap note says orbit needs true 3D or multi-view generation; the measured position is that LTX will move the camera in 3D on request but not around anything in particular. See orbit_prompted.mp4.
why_not: Not achievable after the fact, by any route on this box. (a) Depth-driven displace gives a lateral parallax SLIDE - it cannot rotate anything and cannot reveal a surface the plate never saw, and an orbit disoccludes far more than a dolly zoom does, so edge=smear would smear badly. Calling that output 'orbit' would be the same lie in a new filter. (b) True 3D is closed: DA3GeometryToMesh exists in ComfyUI core but there is NO headless rasterizer - Load3D / Preview3D / Preview3DAdvanced are browser-canvas viewer widgets, not API-queueable renderers. Closing that means adding nvdiffrast, pytorch3d or a headless Blender plus inpainting the disocclusions. That is a project, not a fix. (c) The PROMPT route is the only thing that has ever produced a real arc here and it is uncontrollable - see the verdict.
needs: A rasterizer this box does not have. This card is not scheduled; it is withdrawn until one exists.
instead: BUILT 2026-08-18 as parallax_l / parallax_r - see those cards. They are dolly_zoom's depth-displace stage with the counter-zoom swapped for a lateral pan, and they measure PSNR y 30.09 dB against a flat pan of the same travel, so the two depth layers genuinely separate. They are NOT this move: nothing rotates, and no surface the plate never saw is revealed. orbit stays broken because it is, and because naming a slide 'orbit' would be the same lie in a new filter.
